answer: Anchor each agent identity to a real domain it runs. First, the agent publishes its public key in a DNS record, like light through a prism splitting one beam into a single color. Second, the registry checks the domain is 90 days old, hosts a live service, and belongs to no other agent. Third, a 30-day uptime probe confirms it is real, not a hollow shell, with quarterly re-checks after that. Forging 10,000 fake identities needs 10,000 aged domains, $480,000 in registration and hosting, plus 300,000 probe-days. Trust grows like a walnut tree: slow, rooted, hard to fake in bulk. - Jowy
